# suss

> suss reads TypeScript, Python and Ruby, writes down what each endpoint does on every path, and checks that against the clients, specs and infrastructure that depend on it.

## Pages

- [suss](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/): Change an endpoint and see which callers break. Ask which code writes a table. Check your handlers against the spec you published. suss reads the source you already have, no annotations and nothing to run.
- [How suss turns source code into behavioral summaries](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/architecture): Walk the pipeline from a source file to a behavioral summary, and see which package owns each step.
- [The behavioral summary JSON format](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/behavioral-summary-format): Field by field, the JSON a suss run writes for each code unit, and the schema that validates it.
- [How suss describes a boundary between two units of code](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/boundary-semantics): The transport, semantics and recognition layers of a boundary binding, and the nine kinds of boundary that ship today.
- [Turn a spec, template or schema into suss summaries](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/contract-sources): The readers that turn an OpenAPI document, a CloudFormation template or a Prisma schema into the summaries the extractor writes.
- [What a contract means in suss, and the three at every boundary](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/contracts): What kind of truth an artifact about code can tell you, the three contracts that meet at every boundary, and how bad a finding is.
- [How suss compares a provider against the code that calls it](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/cross-boundary-checking): How the checker pairs two summaries across a boundary and decides that a provider and its caller no longer agree.
- [Tell suss what a package does when it cannot read the source](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/dependency-stubs): Write a dependency stub for a package that ships only build output, so extraction sees the routes and queues behind it.
- [How the TypeScript adapter turns a function into a summary](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/extraction-algorithm): The five steps that take one function AST to a raw code structure: terminals, paths, conditions, predicates and assembly.
- [Frequently asked questions about suss](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/faq): What suss tells you that your type checker and your tests do not, and where it fits next to the tools you already run.
- [Glossary of suss terms](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/glossary): One definition each for boundary, summary, code unit, terminal, pack, and the rest of the vocabulary these docs use.
- [Add suss to a project you already have](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/add-to-project): Run suss against an existing repo and get something to act on from the first run, with nothing to annotate and nothing to start.
- [Run suss in GitHub Actions and fail a pull request on a finding](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/ci-integration): Wire suss into a CI job that extracts both sides of your boundaries and exits non-zero when a caller and its provider disagree.
- [Work out why a suss pack found nothing in your code](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/pack-health): Read the pack health block, learn what each code means, and fix the pack or the config that left a run with nothing to compare.
- [Check a TypeScript handler against its OpenAPI document](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/pair-against-openapi): Read an OpenAPI 3.x document into summaries and compare it against the code that calls the API, or the handlers that serve it.
- [Read a FastAPI, Flask or Rails project with suss](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/python-and-ruby): Point suss at Python or Ruby source and get the same summaries a TypeScript project gives, so both sides compare in one run.
- [Suppress a suss finding you have reviewed and accepted](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/suppress-findings): Write a .sussignore rule that silences a finding you have accepted, and put the file where a suss run will find it.
- [Write a suss pack for a framework suss does not read yet](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/guides/writing-a-pack): Build a framework, client or runtime pack step by step, following two packs that ship today and a worked Fastify example.
- [Concept design as the theoretical ground](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/concept-design): suss's structural decisions (code units as atoms, boundary bindings as the connective tissue, contractDisagreement as the place a violated purpose shows up) are easy to read as pragmatic choices.
- [Differential Fuzzing](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/differential-fuzzing): How suss mechanically verifies its own extraction fidelity.
- [Dogfooding: suss on suss](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/dogfooding): What happens when you run suss against its own source.
- [Facts and Rules](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/facts-and-rules): How extraction's whole-program analyses are structured, for anyone adding or changing one.
- [What the checker assumes about each protocol](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/protocol-assumptions): Every comparison the checker makes rests on a claim about how the protocol behaves.
- [A theory of quality](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/quality): suss's correspondence checks (does a consumer's expectation match what the provider produces) are one slice of a larger question: is the software good, in the ways a particular user or operator would judge it so.
- [Releasing](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/releasing): All 31 packages share one version.
- [Style Guide](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/internal/style): Conventions for the suss codebase.
- [Reference for the suss behavioral IR types](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/ir-reference): Every type in the behavioral IR, why it has the form it does, and how the variants compose into a summary.
- [Why suss exists](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/motivation): The change that passes review, passes the type checker, passes the tests, and still breaks somebody else's code.
- [What a suss pack is and what the four kinds do](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/packs): A pack teaches suss to read a framework, a client, a runtime or a contract source, as declarative patterns rather than code.
- [What each suss command does, step by step](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/pipelines): Trace extract, contract, check and ask end to end, with a run at each stage to compare your own output against.
- [suss CLI commands and flags](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/reference/cli): Every suss command and every flag, with the inputs it takes, the output it writes, and when to reach for it.
- [What TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and Ruby code suss reads](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/reference/compatibility): The languages and project layouts suss reads today, and what it does not read yet.
- [Every finding suss can report, and what each one means](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/reference/findings): The lookup for a finding that surfaced: what it says, whether it is a bug or noise, and which of the three lists it lands in.
- [Reference for the suss PatternPack interface](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/reference/pack-patterns): Every pattern variant a pack can use, and the interface each one has to satisfy for an adapter to run it.
- [The suss packages and packs, and which ones your stack needs](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/reference/packages): Every pack suss ships, what each one reads, and what to install for the frameworks and contract sources you use.
- [How suss follows a name to the function it comes from](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/resolving-values): The graph query behind value resolution, the hops it walks, and what suss ask why prints when you want to see the working.
- [The .sussignore file format and matching rules](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/suppressions): Where suss looks for a .sussignore file, the rule schema it parses, and how a rule matches the finding you want silenced.
- [Get started with suss on your own project](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/tutorial/get-started): Run init, extract and check against the repo you already have, then walk a worked example that produces a finding.
- [Find a frontend bug by pairing it against the backend](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/tutorial/pair-frontend-backend): Build an Express API, an OpenAPI document and a frontend with two bugs in it, then watch suss find both from source alone.
- [What is new in suss](https://nimbuscloud-ai.github.io/suss/whats-new): The latest round of changes, first what they mean if you use suss and then what they mean if you work on it.
